title: Available Energy and Ground States of Convective Hydrodynamic and Hydromagnetic Instabilities
summary: We propose a method for predicting the nonlinear saturation level of convective instabilities in neutral and magnetized fluids. The method combines Gardner's restacking algorithm, which computes the available energy and ground states of collisionless plasmas in phase space, and Lagrangian relaxation, where fluid elements find lower-energy equilibria while preserving local invariants. For the incompressible Rayleigh-Taylor instability, the problem is formally equivalent to Gardner's and the restacking algorithm directly applies in configuration space. To treat compressibility, we follow restacking with Lagrangian relaxation to obtain the ground state, and the results show excellent agreement with direct numerical simulations. Successful extension to the $m=0$ interchange instability in a Z-pinch demonstrates the method's potential as a general framework for estimating the nonlinear extent of convective instabilities, which can facilitate the design and operation of fusion reactors.

title: Operator Formalism for Laser–Plasma Mode Coupling
summary: In this paper, we develop an operator-based framework for laser--plasma wakefield acceleration (LPWA) in capillary discharges, providing a compact and systematic description of the coupled dynamics of laser fields and plasma response. The formalism employs key operators: the transverse modal operator $\hat{K}$, the nonlinear plasma operator $\hat{N}[Ψ]$, the plasma oscillation operator $\hatΩ_p^{\,2}$, and the ponderomotive source operator $\hatα$, which together describe mode coupling, plasma oscillations, and nonlinear feedback induced by the ponderomotive force. In the linear regime, the system is characterized by invariant subspaces associated with stable modal structures, while nonlinear interactions break these invariances, leading to mode mixing and complex dynamics. The approach establishes a direct connection between LPWA and Hilbert-space operator theory, including the invariant subspace, providing a formal mathematical interpretation of energy transfer and wakefield formation. Furthermore, the operator formalism integrates with neural operator methods, allowing efficient approximation of $\hat{N}$ and $\hatα$ for reduced-order modeling and predictive control. This hybrid physics--AI framework offers a robust foundation for modeling, analysis, and optimization of high-intensity laser--plasma interactions in next-generation accelerator experiments.

formal_metadata.abstract: <jats:p>In this paper, we develop an operator-based framework for laser–plasma interactions, providing a compact and systematic description of the coupled dynamics of laser fields and plasma response, with particular relevance to laser wakefield acceleration (LWFA). The formalism employs key operators: the transverse modal operator K^, the nonlinear plasma operator N^[Ψ], the plasma oscillation operator Ω^p2, and the ponderomotive source operator α^, which together describe mode coupling, plasma oscillations, and nonlinear feedback induced by the ponderomotive force. In the linear regime, the system is characterized by invariant subspaces associated with stable modal structures, while nonlinear interactions break these invariances, leading to mode mixing. The operators are defined on explicit Hilbert spaces. We establish the unitarity of linear propagation, the conservation of modal power under the nonlinear flow, the equivalence between the operator and PDE descriptions, and an explicit error bound for finite-mode truncations. We also characterize invariant subspaces through selection rules. Local well-posedness of the nonlinear problem is established under stated regularity assumptions. A reduced two-mode model is validated against direct numerical integration of the paraxial equation, and its accuracy and computational cost are quantified, the validation does not cover wakefield generation (transient plasma wave, pump depletion, injection or acceleration). The formalism provides a unified operator-based framework for the cold-fluid Maxwell–plasma model.</jats:p>

title: Identification of rippling interface between laser-ablated plasma and ambient uniform plasma at rest
summary: We present laboratory experiments on the early stage of the formation process of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks using laser-produced plasmas in an ambient uniform nitrogen (N) gas with 1~Torr under the external magnetic field with controlled polarity. An expanding aluminum (Al) piston plasma arising from laser irradiation interacts with a magnetized ambient N plasma, producing a bright, asymmetric self-emission whose global morphology reverses with the magnetic-field polarity. Two-dimensional ideal-magnetohydrodynamics simulations reproduce the main features of the observed structures and indicate that the ripple formation is unlikely to be driven by the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability, but is instead associated with vortex formation at the rounded leading edge of the piston plasma. We show that the bright, rippling emission delineates the Al-N interface, whose intrinsic width is consistent with an electron kinetic scale, and that its upstream side is predominantly composed of N plasma. This identification allows the formation of a supercritical collisionless shock in the magnetized N plasma to be discussed with minimal Al contamination.

title: Bright Compton source based on the interaction of an ultraintense laser pulse with a relativistically transparent foil and a plasma mirror
summary: We propose and numerically study an x-ray source in which a single laser pulse first accelerates electrons while passing through a relativistically transparent thin overdense foil and then, after reflection from a plasma mirror, collides head-on with them. Two-dimensional kinetic simulations show that for a laser pulse with an intensity of the order of $10^{21}$~W/cm$^2$ and optimal foil parameters, electrons are accelerated to energies of the order of 100~MeV, and the source can deliver up to $10^{7}$ photons per 0.1\% bandwidth per joule of laser energy in the 10--250~keV range, two orders of magnitude more than a similar gas-jet scheme. This also exceeds the spectral yield per joule of the best gas-target betatron sources by about an order of magnitude and is comparable to the best experimental results obtained with near-critical-density targets.

title: Laser wakefield acceleration and x-ray emission in plasma produced by the electrical explosion of an aluminum wire
summary: Underdense plasmas used in relativistic laser-plasma interactions are conventionally produced from gaseous targets, whereas low-density metallic plasmas remain comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate the interaction of a femtosecond petawatt laser with expanded aluminum plasma using particle-in-cell simulations based on an experimentally motivated exploding-wire density profile. Three-dimensional simulations show that the laser propagates through the low-density metallic plasma, drives a pronounced wake-like structure, accelerates electrons to near-GeV energies, and produces directional broadband x-ray emission. Charge-state-resolved diagnostics further show that electrons associated with higher aluminum ionization stages are disproportionately represented in the energetic population. Complementary two-dimensional simulations indicate that the net electron energy gain is dominated by longitudinal electric-field work and show that relativistic electron generation persists under variations of the assumed initial ionization and density conditions, although the yield remains quantitatively sensitive to the plasma state. These results demonstrate the feasibility of electrically exploded aluminum plasma as a target platform for laser wakefield acceleration and associated x-ray generation.

title: Accelerating high-fidelity gyrokinetic fusion simulations with iGENE
summary: We present the latest version of iGENE, a differentiable implementation of the local (flux-tube) gyrokinetic code GENE, now fully rewritten in JAX. iGENE features a multispecies, collisional, fully electromagnetic nonlinear gyrokinetic model while preserving end-to-end differentiability. The code is verified against GENE for linear ITG, TEM and KBM physics and for nonlinear turbulent fluxes with adiabatic and kinetic electrons. Forward-mode derivatives of the linear growth rate agree with finite differences for all five parameters tested, resolving the 30--50\% discrepancy in $\hat{s}$ and $ε$ reported for the earlier TensorFlow version. All collectives are native JAX operations, and the code strong-scales from 2 to 32 H100 GPUs with 86\% parallel efficiency. We then assess three routes to a shorter time to solution. Custom CUDA FFT kernels operating in bfloat16 are up to $3.97\times$ faster than fp32 cuFFT on the transforms, and on a single H100 iGENE is $2.63\times$ faster per time step than single-precision GENE. Multi-rate sub-cycling of the parallel dynamics yields a further $1.89\times$ speedup with kinetic electrons. Finally, a Hermite-Laguerre velocity-space representation is implemented, offering tunable fidelity.
